newsitem.title: USA: US crudes stage buying spree, outrights at $22 bbl.
newsitem.headline: US crudes stage buying spree, outrights at $22 bbl.

text.p: Sharp gains on the NYMEX futures market left cash crude outright prices at extremely lofty heights Friday, over $22.00 a barrel for June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing.
Late talk put June WTI/Cushing at $22.05-15 a barrel, 80 cents stronger than late Thursday.

Paper markets advanced dramatically in the final stages of NYMEX trading hitting session highs at $22.40 a barrel for front June futures. Traders said technical buying in a light volume market pushed paper values.
In addition, continued jitters resulting from the Turkish incursion into northern Iraq, to battle anti-Turkish Kurdish factions, generated buying, traders said.
"It was so thin in there, that locals (NYMEX) seemed to be looking for the run-up, and talked about this Kurdish thing for an excuse," said one cash trader.
Futures buying stole the spotlight from cash grade business. Differentials moved little from the morning to late afternoon, except for a fluctuating Postings trade.
June WTI/Cushing Postings Plus sold from $2.00-2.06. June/July spreads moved back into negative territory as July pegged a six to seven cents edge over June.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James hovered around confirmed trades at WTI/Cushing minus three cents, and Midland/WTI stalled at 37 cents under June WTI/Cushing.
Sour grades also stagnated at existing levels, trading at WTI/Cushing -$1.38 for West Texas Sour/Midland and Eugene Island attracted deals at $1.60 under benchmark.
Sweet grades lost ground as the week progressed, suffering from wide Brent-WTI arbitrage spreads, leading to more opportunities for Brent deliveries to the U.S. Gulf.
June exchange for physicals (EFP's) continued to lose ground, but that was a function of demand slowing after a rush of buying in the previous sessions.

Traders continued to talk of their expectations for foreign crude deliveries against the June NYMEX contract. One trader said as much as one million barrels of fresh Bonny Light would be delivered against paper matches.
There was further talk that refiners who were delivered against in May would refloat their foreign barrels for profit in June.
When the May NYMEX contract expired, a total of 2.73 million barrels of Bonny Light, Brent and Oseberg was delivered against paper contracts, a highly unusual event.
For June, the trend has been to avoid getting stuck with foreign crude that refiners may not be able to run and importantly avoid paying the 60 cents premium for Bonny Light delivered barrels.
In July, the Bonny Light premium will be trimmed to a less drastic 40 cents.
For now, EFP's guarantee buyers WTI deliveries. Active demand pushed June EFP's out to 11-13 cents earlier this week, but prices retreated to current levels at plus 5-6 cents.
"I think everbody who wanted to get their EFP's done have already done so," said a cash trader.
